screens.current_state: apps/web/app/(shell)/storyboards/[id]/page.tsx is a server-rendered, form-driven CRUD scaffold: a 3-column grid (Library tray of ContentBlocks only | section list with manual create-section/create-slot forms | diagnostics+snapshots+comments stack). gaps.title: No three-panel canvas layout (collapsible library | canvas | slide inspector)
gaps.description: Design (routes_storyboard_v2.jsx RouteStoryboardWorkspaceV2, storyboard-workspace.png) uses a responsive 3-panel grid: collapsible left Content Library (260px/44px collapsed), center canvas of sections, and a right slide-inspector aside (320px) that only appears when a slot is selected. Current page.tsx uses a static `xl:grid-cols-[280px_minmax(0,1.4fr)_360px]` layout where the third column is always a diagnostics/snapshot/comment stack, not a per-slide inspector, and the left column is never collapsible. There is no click-to-select-slide state at all.

gaps.title: Missing selected-slot inspector panel (Details/Notes/Meta/Activity/AI tabs)
gaps.description: Design's right sidebar, once a content-unit chip is clicked, shows a sticky inspector with large preview, Edit/Swap/External/More actions, and 5 tabs: Details (owner, last edited, confidence, freshness badge, used-in count, variants list with match %, audience-fit bars per persona, tags), Notes (speaker notes + regenerate + threaded comments + add-comment box), Meta (ID/type/template/dimensions/layout/created/modified/derived-from/collection/access/approved-by/brand/rights/a11y badges), Activity (chronological actor+action+timestamp feed incl. AI actions), and AI (assistant summary + suggestion cards with Apply buttons + ask-about-this-slide input). None of this exists in the current implementation; SlotCard only renders a static thumbnail, a swap form with raw UUID inputs, and slot-anchored comments inline.

gaps.title: No storyboard toolbar (Reorder / Metrics / Filters / AI Rebalance / Track changes)
gaps.description: Design's canvas toolbar row sits above the section list: bold 'Storyboard' label + section count, then right-aligned buttons Reorder, Metrics, Filters, AI Rebalance (AI-tinted), and a 'Track changes' checkbox. Current implementation has no toolbar at all above CreateSectionForm.

gaps.title: Header missing version chip, editing badge, autosave indicator, collaborator avatars, compare/save-version actions
gaps.description: Design title bar shows: title + version chip (v3.2) + 'Editing' AI-tinted badge, a subtitle line 'Auto-saved 2m ago · 6 sections · 22 units · 19 min', an avatar stack of collaborators with '+3' overflow, and action buttons 'Compare to v3.1', 'Save Version', 'Publish' (primary). Current PageHeader only shows eyebrow/title/description text plus a tiny inline snapshot-label form and a 'Publish review' link — no version chip, no editing/collab presence, no compare action, no aggregate counts (sections/units/estimated minutes) in the header.

gaps.title: Bottom metrics strip absent (Storyboard Health, Coverage, Duplicates, Weak Transitions, Read Time, Narrative)
gaps.description: Design renders a 6-column metrics card below the canvas: Storyboard Health (score+descriptor), Content Coverage (%), Duplicates (count + 'Review them' link), Weak Transitions (count + link), Read Time (minutes vs target), Narrative (score + descriptor). Current DiagnosticsPanel only shows a single narrative score badge plus a flat list of warning objects (code/message) with no categorized counts, no coverage %, no duplicate/weak-transition counters, and no read-time metric — largely because the backend analyze() only returns narrativeScore + warnings, not these aggregates (see api_needs).

gaps.title: Section cards lack thumbnail chip grid, per-section stats, and 'used in' / health readouts
gaps.description: Design section row layout is a 4-column grid: drag handle | section meta (numbered badge, title, edit icon, description, units/estMin) | wrapped grid of content-unit thumbnail chips (each with drag handle, type icon, SlideThumb, kind label, match-score %) plus a dashed 'Add content unit / drop from library' drop zone | a right-hand 'Used in' column showing matching-work-product count, a Health meter (%), and an overflow menu. Current StoryboardSectionCard instead renders a plain header (Section N, title, summary, slot-count tag) and a 2-column grid of SlotCard divs with a manual add-slot form; there is no per-chip match score, no drag handle, no 'used in' count, no per-section health meter, and no section edit/overflow menu.

gaps.title: No drag-and-drop for sections or slots; no 'Insert Section' affordance
gaps.description: Design supports draggable section reordering (drag handles, dragOver reflow, opacity/scale/shadow feedback) and thin 'Insert Section' hover-to-expand dividers between every section (plus an 'Add section / AI Suggest' footer). Current implementation has no drag interactions anywhere and section creation is only via a single top form (CreateSectionForm) with a manual numeric orderIndex field; there is no insert-between-sections UI and no AI-suggest-section entry point.

gaps.title: Content Library tray is ContentBlocks-only with no search, tabs, filters, or AI context hint
gaps.description: Design's left Content Library aside has: a search input ('Search content units…' with a '/' kbd hint), three tabs (Recommended/Recent/Library[collections]) with counts, filter chips (All/Slides/Charts/+3), an AI-tinted context hint block ('Matched to Our Solution · CIO audience · Acme Corp' + 'Adjust context'), a scrollable 2-col chip grid of draggable items with kind icon + match %, and a footer with 'New Unit' and 'AI Generate' buttons. Current LibraryTray is a static, non-collapsible card listing only ContentBlocks (via listContentBlocks) with a title + member-count tag and a link — no ContentUnits, no search, no tabs, no filters, no drag source, no AI hint, no add/generate actions.

gaps.title: Adding/swapping slot content requires typing a raw UUID instead of picking from the library
gaps.description: CreateSlotForm and SlotCard's swap form both require the user to paste a 'selectedObjectId' UUID into a text input and choose an object-type dropdown. The design's entire interaction model is click/drag a library chip onto a slot or drop-zone — there is no equivalent 'type a UUID' affordance anywhere in the mockups. This is a fundamental interaction-model gap, not just missing polish.

gaps.title: Gap slot placeholder styling differs from 'Recommendation needed' design treatment
gaps.description: Current gap slots render a plain dashed-amber box with the text 'Recommendation needed'. Design instead shows an 'Add content unit / or drop from library' dashed drop-zone tile styled like the other chips (not amber-alarm colored) — gaps in the design are a neutral empty-slot invitation, not a warning-colored callout. Low/medium visual mismatch in tone and affordance.

gaps.title: Comments list has no threading, resolve state, or type filter
gaps.description: Design's comments panel (top-right in the mockups' surrounding shell, and the Notes tab in the slide inspector) shows unresolved/all-types filter dropdowns, per-comment avatar + timestamp + reply count/affordance, and a persistent add-comment composer per slide. Current CommentList/StoryboardCommentForm render a flat list of comment bodies with an anchor label only (no avatar, no timestamp, no reply thread, no resolved/unresolved toggle) even though the Comment schema exposes parentCommentId and status which are unused here.

gaps.title: Snapshot panel lacks approval-state actions and diff/compare view
gaps.description: SnapshotPanel lists snapshots and shows a selected-snapshot summary (label, frozen counts, approvalState text) but exposes no action to change approvalState (approve/reject) and no way to compare two snapshots side-by-side, whereas the design's header includes an explicit 'Compare to v3.1' button implying a diff view is a first-class capability.

gaps.title: Restricted / not-found / error states are plain text-only, no visual parity with rest of app
gaps.description: RestrictedStoryboard, StoryboardNotFound, and StoryboardError are implemented (a genuine strength versus the design, which shows no such states), but they are minimal single-card layouts with no illustration, no suggested next actions beyond a create form / storyboards list, and no consistent icon/badge treatment matching the rest of the redesigned shell (e.g., no status chip styling parity once the visual system is upgraded elsewhere). Low severity since functionally correct — flag for visual-consistency pass once the shared UI kit is upgraded.

screens.current_state: Home (`apps/web/app/(shell)/page.tsx`) is a fully static server component rendering hardcoded demo data (`features/demo/data.ts`) via a generic marketing-style PageHeader, four stat cards, a work-products/reviews/storyboard-snapshot two-column section, and a content-families grid — none of it calls the live API despite equivalent endpoints existing (reviews, admin health, work-products, content-units, storyboards families). Plays (`plays/page.tsx`) and Opportunities (`opportunities/page.tsx`) are explicit "Preview-only module" placeholders confirmed by their own copy and by the complete absence of Play/Opportunity concepts anywhere in the PRD/architecture docs (`docs/01`–`docs/07`) or backend routes (`services/api/app/api/routes` has no plays.py or opportunities.py) — Plays shows 4 static cards with no detail route, and Opportunities shows a 2-card static summary. The design (routes_3.jsx/routes_4.jsx + plays-detail-view.png mockup) specs both as fully interactive, richly data-driven screens: a personalized Home briefing with an AI-suggestions panel and cross-entity attention feed, a tabbed/filterable Plays list driving into a full Play Detail workspace (stats bar, flow steps, AI guidance rail), and a multi-pane Opportunity Workspace (deal health, team activity, AI play/slide recommendations, drag-drop Play Builder).

gaps.title: Home dashboard is 100% static mock data with no API wiring or loading/error/empty states
gaps.description: apps/web/app/(shell)/page.tsx imports everything from features/demo/data.ts (stats, workProducts, reviewItems, storyboardSections, contentFamilies) and never calls lib/api.ts. Backend endpoints already exist that could power equivalent sections: GET /api/reviews/items + /api/reviews/queues (Reviews needing judgment), GET /api/admin/health (catalog/ingestion health), GET /api/work-products/families (Active ingestion list), GET /api/content-units/families (Family-first content signal), GET /api/storyboards + snapshots (Storyboard snapshot card). None are used, and there is no loading skeleton, error state, or empty state anywhere on the page.

gaps.title: Home is missing the 'BoxBrain suggests' AI panel entirely
gaps.description: Design Home (routes_4.jsx RouteHome) places a distinctive ai-panel card next to 'Needs your attention': gradient/tinted border, Sparkle icon + 'BoxBrain suggests' + BETA badge, and 3 bulleted AI suggestion rows each ending in a 'Take action' button. Current Home has no AI-suggestion surface on the dashboard at all — 'Ask BoxBrain' only appears as a header CTA link to a different route.

gaps.title: Home header is generic marketing copy, not the personalized daily-briefing greeting
gaps.description: Design shows 'Good morning, Sarah' as an H1 plus a dated context line ('Here's what's moving across your accounts today — {date}'). Current PageHeader instead renders a fixed eyebrow/title/description ('Governed content graph' / 'BoxBrain operating console' / static blurb) with Browse Library + Ask BoxBrain buttons — no personalization, no date, no per-user framing.

gaps.title: 'Needs your attention' cross-entity feed is missing; current split is not equivalent

Current Home instead has a reviews-only 'Reviews needing judgment' card (plain badges, no icon chips, no color coding, no chevron) plus a separate, unrelated 'Storyboard snapshot' card — Opportunity/Play items can't appear since no backend exists for those entities.

gaps.title: Missing 'Quick links' 4-up tile row on Home
gaps.description: Design renders a 4-card icon+label+chevron quick-nav row (Ask BoxBrain, Browse Library, Open Plays, My Opportunity). Current Home only exposes 2 of these as PageHeader action buttons (Browse library, Ask BoxBrain); there is no card-grid quick-nav section and no links to Plays/Opportunities from Home at all.

gaps.title: StatCard has no sparkline trend chart
gaps.description: Design's stat-card renders an inline SVG sparkline (up/down colored trend line) beneath the hint text on every metric — used on Home's quick stats and on the Play Detail stats bar. components/ui.tsx StatCard has no spark prop/element at all, and no sparkline primitive exists anywhere in the shared UI kit.

gaps.title: Plays has no Play Detail route at all
gaps.description: apps/web/app/(shell)/plays/ contains only page.tsx (the list) — there is no plays/[id]/page.tsx, and the list cards are not clickable to a detail page (only a generic 'View related storyboard' link is present, pointing at an unrelated storyboard). The design's Play Detail screen (routes_3.jsx RoutePlayDetail, confirmed by uploads/plays-detail-view.png) is an entire workspace: breadcrumb trail, hero card (gradient icon, VERIFIED badge, title+favorite star, tag chips, owner block, last-updated), a 5-metric stats bar with sparklines (Usage/Win Rate/Avg Deal Size Increase/Time to Value/Adoption), a 4-column info band (Intended Audience/Use Cases/When to Use/Success Criteria), a tab bar (Play Flow/Rationale/Related Opportunities 24/Assets 18/Outcome Metrics/Reviews 8), a numbered 'Recommended Flow' step list with type badges (MEETING/WORK PRODUCT/WORKSHOP/ENGAGEMENT/PROPOSAL) and per-step duration, and a sticky right rail (AI Guidance panel, Similar Plays list, Actions menu with Duplicate/Customize/Publish/Share/Export/Archive). None of this exists in the current implementation.

gaps.title: Plays list is missing category filter tabs and differs on header actions
gaps.description: Design's RoutePlaysList shows filter tabs with counts (All Plays 28 / Growth 12 / Expansion 7 / Cross-Sell 5 / Retention 4) plus 'Filter' and primary 'New Play' header buttons. Current /plays has no tabs/categories at all and replaces the header actions with a single disabled-looking 'Limited preview' lock button, consistent with the product's preview framing but with no filtering affordance whatsoever.

gaps.title: Play cards use a uniform icon/generic tags instead of design's varied iconography and real stats row
gaps.description: Current Plays cards all render the same blue-50 tile with a BookOpen icon and generic Tag chips (Preview / N steps / N uses) built from array index math. Design varies the icon tile per play (gradient background, differing icon: mountain/trending-up/rocket by index%3), shows a VERIFIED badge only on the flagship play, and renders a real stats footer (uses count with trending icon, win-rate % with check icon) instead of placeholder tags.

gaps.title: Opportunities page is a 2-card summary; design specs an entire multi-pane Opportunity Workspace
gaps.description: apps/web/app/(shell)/opportunities/page.tsx renders only a hero summary card (name, headline, Meter fit score, tags, one CTA) and a 4-item static recommendations list. Design's RouteOpportunity (routes_3.jsx) is a full workspace: header row with status badge, stage/close-date/amount, avatar-stack of team members + overflow count, Share/More actions; a tab bar (Workspace/Storyboard/Insights/Requirements 24/Messages 8/Activity); and a 4-column body — (1) Context Snapshot (customer/industry/regions/owner/solution/decision-criteria/pain-points) + Deal Health score-circle with factor badges (engagement/budget/competition/timeline) + Team & Collaboration activity feed with avatars/timestamps/quoted comments, (2) BoxBrain AI recommendation mini-cards + ranked 'Top Plays' list with match-score chips + 'Top Slides' ranked table with a relevance color legend, (3) Saved Candidate Materials file list with match scores + drag-drop upload dropzone, (4) a drag-and-drop Play Builder (Build/Review/Finalize stepper, reorderable Sections list, reorderable slide Content list, Preview/Compare/Publish Pack actions). None of these panes exist today.

gaps.title: No backend data model exists for any Opportunity Workspace concept
gaps.description: grep of services/api/app/api/routes finds no plays.py or opportunities.py, and no PRD/architecture doc (docs/01-07) mentions Play or Opportunity entities — confirming these are out of current backend scope. Design requires: an Opportunity record (stage/close-date/team/tags), Deal Health scoring, AI-driven Play/Slide recommendation ranking with match scores, a Team & Collaboration activity feed, and Play Builder/Artifact Pack composition+publish. All are absent; lib/api.ts has zero Play/Opportunity-specific client functions.

gaps.title: Opportunities page has no tab navigation
gaps.description: Design's tab bar (Workspace/Storyboard/Insights/Requirements/Messages/Activity) is entirely absent from the current page, which is a single static view. The one interactive affordance ('Open opportunity storyboard preview') routes to a generic, non-opportunity-scoped storyboard rather than an Opportunity-specific Storyboard tab.

gaps.title: Recommendation list styling doesn't reuse the app's trust/relevance indicator system
gaps.description: Current 'Top preview recommendations' renders plain rows with a placeholder 'Recommendation is read-only in MVP.' caption. Design's equivalent (Top Plays / Top Slides) uses match-score chips, a 'Best Match' badge, and a ranked table with a High/Medium/Low relevance color-dot legend — visual language already used elsewhere in the design system but not reused here.

screens.current_state: apps/web/app/(shell)/ask/page.tsx implements a generic 3-column engineering-search UI: a single-line query input + Ask/Search endpoint toggle, a left 'Filters' card (profile/object-type/governance/freshness/result-mode selects + debug toggle), a flat undifferentiated list of SearchResultCard results in the middle, and a right column with a client-only 'Saved searches' list and a raw JSON 'Debug' panel. It is API-wired to POST /api/search and /api/ask and has solid loading/empty/error/restricted states. It shares no code with the design's Ask BoxBrain screen beyond fetching the same endpoints.

gaps.title: Overall page layout does not match design's 2-column composer+results / selection-tray structure
gaps.description: Design (routes_1.jsx RouteAskBoxBrain) is a 2-column grid: main column (H1 'Ask BoxBrain' + sparkle icon, subtitle, 'How it works' link, a prominent AI query panel, 'Top results' header + tabs, sectioned result groups) and a fixed 340px right-hand 'My selection' tray. Current page.tsx instead renders PageHeader (generic copy) + a 3-column '.three-col' grid (Filters sidebar | results | saved-searches/debug). None of the design's visual hierarchy, spacing, or section grouping is present.

gaps.title: Query composer is a plain text input, not the design's AI panel with embedded controls, filter chips, and example queries
gaps.description: Design shows a bordered 'ai-panel': a 2-row textarea with placeholder 'Ask BoxBrain anything…', an embedded send button and mic button positioned inside the input, a row of removable/expandable filter chips (Content type, Industry: Financial Services [active, with X], Date, More filters), and a 'Try an example' row of 4 clickable example-query chips that populate the query. Current implementation has a single-line <input> in a bordered label with an external Button for submit, no mic control, no inline filter chips, no example chips, and instead exposes a raw 'Ask'/'Search' endpoint-choice toggle (a backend implementation detail not present in the design at all).

gaps.title: Results are a flat undifferentiated list; missing result-count header, sort/view controls, type tabs, and per-type sections
gaps.description: Design shows: 'Top results' + '128 results' count, 'Sort by: Relevance' + grid/list View toggle, then tabs 'All 128 / Slides 48 / Work Products 41 / Plays 39' with count badges, then content grouped into labeled sections (SLIDES as a 3-up card grid with 'See all N' link, WORK PRODUCTS as a row list with 'See all N' link, implicitly Plays too), plus a 'Show more' pagination control at the bottom. Current page.tsx renders none of this: no header/count, no sort/view toggle, no tabs, no per-type sectioning — just one column of SearchResultCard mapped from a single filtered array regardless of result type.

gaps.title: Result card visual language doesn't differentiate Slide vs Work Product results and is missing key visual elements
gaps.description: Design's SLIDES cards show: rank badge (#1) on the top result, a page-count overlay chip ('18 slides'), title, date + version ('May 7, 2024 · v3'), status badges (Approved/Fresh/Canonical), and AI signal chips with icons (High semantic match, Reused often, Recently used, Recently used). Design's WORK PRODUCTS rows show: file-type icon, title, kind + date, owner Avatar, status badges, a horizontal match-bar with percentage (not just a score pill), and an overflow/kebab menu. Current SearchResultCard renders one generic card shape for every result: 170px thumbnail, title, ScorePill, ExternalLink icon, summary snippet, a single type Tag, status badges, and explanationChips shown as plain AI badges — no rank badge, no match-bar/Meter (a Meter component already exists in ui.tsx but is unused here), no owner avatar, no kebab menu, no date/version line.

gaps.title: SearchResultItem API schema cannot supply per-item date/version/owner or aggregate/tab counts
gaps.description: services/api/app/schemas/api.py SearchResultItem only has objectType, objectId, resultGrain, title, summary, previewUri, score, explanationChips, statusChips — no createdAt/updatedAt/versionLabel/owner fields, and SearchResponse has no total count or per-object-type counts (needed for the 'Top results / 128 results' line and the All/Slides/Work Products/Plays tab counts). ContentUnitVersion-adjacent schemas elsewhere do carry createdAt/updatedAt/versionLabel (services/api/app/schemas/api.py ~lines 316-353), so that data exists in the domain but isn't projected into search results; no owner/author field exists anywhere in the schema layer.

gaps.title: AI signal chips are generic match-type labels, not the design's usage-based signals, and no reuse/recency tracking exists
gaps.description: use_cases._component_explanation_chips only emits mechanical labels ('keyword match', 'semantic match', 'metadata match', 'approved/trusted', 'family rollup'/'variant rollup'/'version match', 'N matching versions'). Design's per-slide signal chips read 'High semantic match', 'Reused often', 'Recently used' — the latter two require reuse-frequency and recency-of-use tracking that does not exist anywhere in the backend (no usage_count/reused/last-used fields found in domain models or schemas).

gaps.title: Right rail is a bespoke 'Saved searches' + Debug panel; design's session 'My selection' content tray is entirely absent
gaps.description: Design's right rail is a persistent, session-scoped 'My selection' tray: header with item count + close, 'SAVED ITEMS' list (thumbnail, title, type+date, status tags, per-item remove X), 'GENERATED BY BOXBRAIN' section (AI-generated artifact card), 'Add custom content' button, a 'QUICK ACTIONS' 2x2 grid (Compare, Create brief, Export to PPT, Share collection), a primary 'Start a new chat' button, and a footer note ('Selections are saved to this session'). None of this exists on the Ask page. The app does have a global 'My Selection' affordance in the topbar (apps/web/components/shell.tsx SelectionTray) but it is only a static link with a hardcoded count of 4 pointing to one fixed storyboard — not an expandable, addable-to tray, and it isn't wired to anything on this screen. Current page instead shows a locally-scoped, non-persistent 'Saved searches' list (query bookmarking, lost on refresh) and a raw JSON debug viewer — a developer-facing feature not present in the design.

gaps.title: Selection tray's Quick Actions have no backend capability
gaps.description: Design's tray Quick Actions (Compare, Create brief, Export to PPT, Share collection) and the underlying idea of a session 'selection'/collection of content that persists and can be acted upon have no backend support. grep of services/api/app/api/routes shows no compare, brief-generation, ppt-export, or share/collection endpoints, and no selection/collection persistence concept anywhere in the schema or use cases.

gaps.title: Filter model is an engineering control panel, not the design's integrated chip-based filtering
gaps.description: Design treats filters as inline chips inside the query composer (Content type, Industry as an active removable chip, Date, More filters) plus clickable example-query chips. gaps.title: Suggested Action panel exposes only 3 of 5 candidate actions instead of always showing all

The backend already exposes all 5 action endpoints (mark-variant, mark-similar, merge-versions, set-canonical, reject) via services/api/app/api/routes/reviews.py, so this is purely a frontend interaction gap, not a backend one.

gaps.title: Provenance Overview card missing from AI/decision sidebar

gaps.title: Full multi-item 'Compare' drawer (slide-compare.png) is entirely unimplemented

gaps.title: Compare drawer's per-item metadata (ratings, usage counts, file size, last-updated-by) has no backend support

backend.summary: The backend (FastAPI + use-case layer) is materially more complete than a scaffold: all 46 OpenAPI paths have matching route handlers, the frontend api.ts client hits real paths that exist, the Alembic chain is a single linear chain (0001->0005, no branching heads), and the dual-mode repository (in-memory default / SQLAlchemy via BOXBRAIN_REPOSITORY=database) uses a consistent duck-typed `_save_*`/`getattr(repository, 'save_x', None)` hook pattern so most governance mutations (approval/freshness/canonical/review actions) correctly persist to Postgres and write audit events when DB mode is active. The real gaps are: (1) pagination is a total placeholder across every list endpoint (nextCursor is hardcoded None everywhere, and the frontend already sends cursor/limit/mode params the backend silently drops), (2) `/api/assets/{key}` has zero actor/visibility enforcement despite every JSON endpoint enforcing restricted-object filtering, (3) the whole frontend runs as `x-boxbrain-user: admin` by default with no in-app role switcher, so restricted-visibility code paths are never exercised in practice, (4) three whole feature domains (build/export manifests, Collections, real AI enrichment/ai_outputs) have SQL tables scaffolded in infra/initial_db_schema.sql but zero ORM models, use-cases, or routes wired to them, and (5) the containerized app stack boots DB mode with `seed=False` and no seed script, so a fresh stack has an empty catalog until someone manually ingests a deck. These findings track closely with (and add concrete code evidence for) the implementation report's own 'Current Known Gaps' section.
contract_drift: GET /api/content-units/families: frontend (listContentUnitFamilies in apps/web/lib/api.ts) sends mode, cursor, limit query params (ContentUnitListMode/ListContentUnitFamiliesInput) but services/api/app/api/routes/content_units.py::list_families and the OpenAPI operation only declare approvalState/freshnessState — FastAPI silently drops the unknown params, so pagination and the families-vs-variants list mode are pure no-ops server-side today.
GET /api/reviews/items: frontend (listReviewItems) sends cursor/limit; routes/reviews.py::list_review_items only accepts queueType/status. Same silent-drop pattern.

GET /api/content-blocks, GET /api/storyboards, GET /api/work-products/families: all return the PageEnvelope shape {items, nextCursor} but no route accepts any pagination parameter, and every use-case method hardcodes nextCursor=None — the PageEnvelope contract is aspirational, not implemented, across the board.

POST /api/reviews/candidates/generate: frontend (generateReviewCandidates) posts a JSON body {queueType, query, limit}; routes/reviews.py::generate_review_candidates declares no request body at all (neither does the OpenAPI operation), and use_cases.generate_review_candidates(actor) ignores any filter, always running a full O(n^2) deterministic sweep over every ContentUnitVersion.

GET /api/admin/audit-events exists in route/use-case/OpenAPI but apps/web never calls it (admin/page.tsx only reads aggregated counts off /api/admin/health's AdminHealth.reviewAudit) — a live but currently unconsumed surface with no pagination/filtering if it is wired up later.

Two divergent get_actor implementations: app/dependencies.py::get_actor (header defaults 'viewer'/None, different header semantics) is dead code that nothing imports; every route actually depends on app/api/dependencies.py::get_actor (different defaults: X-BoxBrain-Role default 'viewer' falls back to X-BoxBrain-User, X-BoxBrain-User-Id default 'seed-viewer'). Not a runtime bug, but a real risk that a future edit lands in the unused copy.

quick_fixes.title: Wire real cursor/limit pagination (and families/variants mode) into list endpoints
quick_fixes.description: Add cursor/limit query params to list_families (plus honoring `mode`), list_review_items, list_content_blocks, list_storyboards, list_work_product_families, and thread them through the corresponding use_cases.list_* methods so nextCursor is real instead of hardcoded None. The frontend already sends these params for content-units/families and reviews/items, so this closes an existing silent drop.

quick_fixes.title: Wire queueType/limit(/query) request body into POST /api/reviews/candidates/generate
quick_fixes.description: The frontend already posts {queueType, query, limit} but the route accepts no body and use_cases.generate_review_candidates(actor) always full-sweeps every ContentUnitVersion via the O(n^2) _deterministic_review_candidates(). Add a request schema, thread queueType/limit into filtering so the Reviews Hub 'generate more' action actually scopes work instead of silently ignoring the payload.

quick_fixes.title: Enforce actor/visibility checks on GET /api/assets/{key}
quick_fixes.description: assets.py never calls get_actor and never checks whether the owning ContentUnit/WorkProduct version is restricted — it just linear-scans stored_objects for a matching metadata['key'] and streams bytes back to anyone. Every JSON endpoint filters restricted objects, but the raw render/thumbnail bytes referenced by renderUri/thumbnailUri bypass that filtering entirely if the key is known. Add get_actor + a restricted-object check (deny or require reviewer+ role) before returning the asset.

quick_fixes.title: Index stored_objects by key instead of linear-scanning on every asset fetch
quick_fixes.description: get_asset() does `for stored_object in use_cases.repository.stored_objects.values(): if stored_object.metadata.get('key') == key` — an O(n) scan per image/thumbnail request. Build/maintain a key->id index (or key as the dict key) so thumbnail-heavy pages (Library, Storyboard, Reviews compare) don't degrade linearly with catalog size.

quick_fixes.title: Make CORS origins configurable via env instead of hardcoded localhost regex
quick_fixes.description: register_middleware() in main.py hardcodes allow_origin_regex to localhost/127.0.0.1 only. Any non-localhost deployment of the containerized app stack (real host/domain, staging URL) will have browser-side API calls silently blocked by CORS with no config knob. Add a BOXBRAIN_CORS_ORIGINS setting (comma-separated) with the current localhost regex as the default.

quick_fixes.title: Remove or clearly deprecate the dead get_actor in app/dependencies.py
quick_fixes.description: app/dependencies.py defines a get_actor with different header semantics than the one actually wired into every route (app/api/dependencies.py). Nothing imports the former; delete it or add a comment redirecting future edits, to avoid someone fixing a role bug in the copy that isn't used.

large_shortfalls.why_large: Current model is a single boolean `restricted` flag per family/version enforced by header-trusted role heuristics (get_actor infers role from X-BoxBrain-User/Role headers with no auth backing them); the frontend's default header hardcodes x-boxbrain-user: admin with no in-app role switcher, so restricted-visibility code paths are effectively never exercised end-to-end today. There is no tenant/org membership table, no per-source ACL, and the `users` table in infra/initial_db_schema.sql has zero ORM model or use-case wiring.
large_shortfalls.plan_hint: Design tenant/org membership + object/source visibility tables, replace header-trusted actor resolution with real auth (OIDC/SSO), and add an in-app role/impersonation switcher for pilot testing before real client content loads. Matches the implementation report's own recommended step 1.

large_shortfalls.capability: AI enrichment workers / real candidate generation pipeline
large_shortfalls.why_large: _deterministic_review_candidates() in use_cases.py is a synchronous O(n^2) text-Jaccard heuristic run inline on-request (no background job, no embeddings/LLM signal, no incremental scan). The `ai_outputs` table exists in the SQL schema (infra/initial_db_schema.sql) but has no ORM model, no repository method, and no use-case ever touches it — AI suggestion provenance/model/confidence metadata described in CLAUDE.md rule #6 has nowhere to persist today.
large_shortfalls.plan_hint: Move candidate generation into an RQ ingestion/enrichment worker stage keyed off embeddings already stored per ContentUnit/WorkProduct version, persist AI outputs (model/prompt/confidence) to a real ai_outputs table, and link accepted/rejected review items back to those rows.

large_shortfalls.why_large: `build_manifests` and `build_manifest_slots` tables are created by migration 0001 (via infra/initial_db_schema.sql) but have zero ORM models (db_models.py), zero repository/use-case methods, zero routes, and zero OpenAPI operations — grep across services/api/app for 'build_manifest'/'BuildManifest' returns nothing outside the raw SQL. The frontend Publish/Package route remains entirely demo-data per the implementation report.
large_shortfalls.plan_hint: Define BuildManifest/BuildManifestSlot domain + SQLAlchemy models, add a snapshot-to-manifest use case off existing immutable Storyboard snapshots, and add export/package preview endpoints — sequencing matches the report's step 5 (needs Storyboard snapshots + WorkProducts + storage, which already exist).

large_shortfalls.why_large: `collections`/`collection_members` tables exist in infra/initial_db_schema.sql but are completely unimplemented — no db_models.py rows, no use-case, no routes; called out explicitly as missing MVP scope for Library in the implementation report.
large_shortfalls.plan_hint: Treat as a net-new small domain slice (family/variant-agnostic saved refs) once visibility model lands, since collection membership will need the same restricted-object filtering as everything else.

large_shortfalls.capability: Generated/typed frontend API client tied to the OpenAPI contract
large_shortfalls.why_large: apps/web/lib/api.ts is a ~1100-line hand-maintained client with no codegen or CI check against contracts/openapi/boxbrain.v2.yaml; the pagination/candidate-generation drift found in this audit is exactly the kind of thing that will keep silently diverging without a generated client or a contract test.
large_shortfalls.plan_hint: Adopt an OpenAPI->TS codegen step in CI (or at minimum a contract test that walks FastAPI's route table against the yaml and api.ts's endpoint strings) so drift fails the build instead of shipping silently.

large_shortfalls.why_large: SqlAlchemyBoxBrainRepository is architecturally an in-memory read-model cache (dict attributes) refreshed via reload(), called once at process startup and then ad hoc only before storyboard section/slot/review mutations (not before content-unit approval/canonical/comment/note mutations). Running more than one API worker process against the same Postgres would let each process's cache diverge (stale reads, lost updates from sibling workers), and reload()'s dict.update() merge semantics never remove rows deleted out-of-band.
large_shortfalls.plan_hint: Either move remaining read paths to direct SQL queries (already flagged as remaining work in the implementation report) or explicitly pin the API to a single worker/process until that migration lands; document the constraint now so nobody scales workers under DB mode by accident.

db_mode_risks: Empty catalog on fresh boot: infra/docker-compose.app.yml sets BOXBRAIN_REPOSITORY=database for the full containerized stack, and dependencies.py constructs SqlAlchemyBoxBrainRepository(SessionLocal, seed=False) — there is no seed/fixture script for Postgres (no `make seed-db`, nothing under any 'seed' path) equivalent to the rich in-memory seed() fixture (ROI/architecture/restricted families, seeded WorkProduct, ContentBlock, Storyboard, review items). A fresh stack boot is empty until someone manually uploads a deck through ingestion — a real problem for demos, smoke tests, or pilot walkthroughs run against the containerized stack.

Hard startup dependency on migration completion with no retry/backoff: `repository` is a module-level singleton built at import time in app/dependencies.py; SqlAlchemyBoxBrainRepository.__init__ calls reload() immediately, which SELECTs from tables that must already exist. infra/docker-compose.app.yml correctly gates the api service on `migrate: condition: service_completed_successfully` and `postgres: condition: service_healthy`, but running the API standalone (e.g. `make api-db`, or a bare uvicorn invocation per README/AGENTS.md examples) without first running `alembic upgrade head` will crash hard at import with no graceful wait or clear remediation message.

Stale-cache risk from reload() merge semantics: reload() populates self.* dicts via `.update(...)`, which adds/overwrites but never removes entries — rows deleted directly in Postgres out-of-band (manual cleanup, another process) will keep appearing as present in a running API process's in-memory read model until restart.

reload() is only invoked ad hoc before storyboard section/slot mutations and review_action/generate_review_candidates (via _refresh_repository()), not before content-unit approval/freshness/canonical, comment, or note mutations — meaning those paths always operate on whatever was loaded at startup or by the last storyboard/review refresh, which is fine for a single in-process demo but is an inconsistency worth documenting before scaling reliance on it.

No connection pool sizing/env exposed in config.py/database.py (create_engine uses SQLAlchemy defaults); combined with the reload()-heavy access pattern (broad SELECT scans triggered by ordinary mutation requests), concurrent pilot load could hit pool exhaustion or slow full-table reloads well before real data volume grows large.

BOXBRAIN_DB_SCHEMA (custom Postgres schema support) only adjusts search_path/version_table_schema; migration 0001 unconditionally runs `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector`/`uuid-ossp` from infra/initial_db_schema.sql — worth explicitly verifying extension creation behavior when a non-default BOXBRAIN_DB_SCHEMA is set, since this path isn't covered by the migration chain's own tests.
